correctness.summary: Partitioning the (n-2)-clique by adjacency to the two outside vertices gives explicit edge-type contributions to the Szeged index and exact Wiener-index formulas in all three adjacency regimes. Solving the resulting equality equations under the exact two-connectivity constraints leaves only the Zhang-Li infinite family and one order-10 sporadic graph. A definition-level verifier matched the closed formulas on 1,160 connected profiles and the equality classification on 8,175 two-connected profiles through order 18.

limitations: The theorem does not classify equality graphs whose clique number is below n-2.
Older chemical-graph literature using different family terminology and recent unindexed work remain residual originality risks.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Zhang and Li explicitly pose the eta(G)=2n equality classification as an open problem, display the infinite K_{n-2}-core family, and note that their sufficient condition is not necessary. Their paper does not classify the K_{n-2}-core regime or give the present exact formulas. The full Bonamy-Knor-Luzar-Pinlou-Skrekovski paper and searches under near-complete, clique-deletion, and Szeged-Wiener terminology revealed no prior equivalent classification. No specific inaccessible source was identified as especially likely to contain it; older terminology and very recent unindexed work remain residual risks.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result solves the new equality problem completely in the natural near-complete class used by the source paper's sharpness construction, shows that its infinite family is unique there except for one n=10 isomorphism type, and supplies exact Szeged-Wiener formulas for every 2-connected graph containing an (n-2)-clique.
